ov: A huge, varied order of fish named for their whisker-like barbels. None have scales. They range from giants like the Mekong giant catfish to the tiny parasitic candiru. Most feed by suction or gulping rather than biting.

why.p: Smaller species such as Corydoras and plecos are popular aquarium fish.
why.ac: Many catfish are nocturnal, though some are active at dusk or by day.
why.et: Many larger species are farmed or fished for food, such as Pangasius.

len: Many under 12 cm; wels catfish over 2.5 m
rg: Inland and coastal waters of every continent except Antarctica; most diverse in tropical South America, Asia and Africa.
df: Varies widely; many are scavenging bottom feeders.
fx: Many cave-dwelling catfish have lost their eyes entirely.
The wels catfish is one of only two catfish native to Europe.
